findings.title: MCP 2026-07-28 is the final baseline
findings.statement: The successor should not inherit MCP-Geo’s default 2025-11-25 runtime. The 2026-07-28 final specification provides the current stateless, routable and self-describing baseline.

findings.title: MCP-Geo is explicitly a learning journal
findings.statement: The repository presents itself as personal research and not production code or a formal proposal. Its 103-tool manifest and broad coupling make it evidence to harvest rather than the successor skeleton.

findings.title: OKF 0.2 is Markdown/YAML, not a JSON runtime schema
findings.statement: The normative core is a directory of Markdown concepts with YAML frontmatter. Explorer descriptors, JSON-LD, YAML-LD and sharded indexes are additive application/publication conventions.

findings.title: Keep OKF descriptive
findings.statement: OKF should describe providers, datasets, capabilities, licences, policies, workflows, lineage, trust, freshness and attested-computation interfaces while referring to runtime authorities.

findings.title: WebMCP remains a draft
findings.statement: WebMCP is a Community Group draft with active API changes and unresolved browser security and lifecycle questions.

findings.title: Constrain WebMCP to open read-only operations
findings.statement: Use it only for catalogue search, facets, record inspection, relationships, map selection and current-view evidence in the demonstrator.

findings.title: ChatGPT Sites is not the protected path
findings.statement: Sites is a beta surface; UK availability and data/inference residency must be checked per current official documentation. It does not evidence the controls needed for PSGA or commercial data.

findings.title: OS OAuth is provider project authentication
findings.statement: For relevant OS APIs, OAuth uses client credentials. It authenticates a project/workload; it does not create delegated user authority.

findings.title: Broker upstream credentials server-side
findings.statement: The platform should authorise the human/agent action itself, then select an organisation-owned provider credential. Provider tokens must not reach browsers or unauthorised clients.

findings.title: HMLR is not one open tier
findings.statement: Price Paid Data is open with additional address-field rights, while title, official-copy, Business Gateway and licensed bulk services have separate access and fee conditions.

findings.title: LandIS provides open discovery but record rights remain specific
findings.statement: The 2026 open-access portal and OGC Records interface support machine discovery. Each product record must still carry its own licence, scale and fitness-for-purpose evidence.

findings.title: ONS data, geography and Nomis are distinct provider lanes
findings.statement: They have different identifiers, interfaces, update cycles, licensing details and statistical/geographic semantics. A single “ONS adapter” would hide important differences.

findings.title: Use deterministic geospatial software
findings.statement: Containment, intersection, transformation, routing, simplification, aggregation and rendering should be performed by tested libraries/services, not inferred by the language model.

findings.title: Treat cache as a governed subsystem
findings.statement: Every cache entry needs provider, dataset/version, source checksum, retrieval time, licence, entitlement, policy version, transformation, expiry, audience and permitted operations.

findings.title: Filter discovery as well as invocation
findings.statement: The policy enforcement path must cover catalogue search, MCP capability listing, workflow initiation, provider credential selection, attribute projection, map generation, export and audit access.

findings.title: Allow decisions should carry obligations
findings.statement: Examples include attribution, feature limits, aggregation, masking, reduced resolution, no persistent export, approval, cost controls, retention and destination constraints.

findings.title: Return a result-level evidence receipt
findings.statement: Every material result should bind actor chain, policy decision, sources, versions, CRS/transformation parameters, software, output hashes, licence obligations and trace context.

findings.title: Do not treat an LLM plan as workflow authority
findings.statement: Use Arazzo or a deterministic workflow model for governed multi-step processes; use Tasks and MRTR for protocol interaction and approval/resumption.

findings.title: Separate the public plane from protected services
findings.statement: A portable static public discovery plane and separate authenticated control/data plane give a safer initial topology than one shared multi-tier deployment.

findings.title: Initial protected users are Entra-managed
findings.statement: The Azure recommendation assumes the first public-sector pilot can use Entra federation and Intune/Conditional Access posture.

findings.title: The first pilot is departmental, not national-scale
findings.statement: Sizing assumes tens to low hundreds of concurrent users, bounded exports and reference datasets in the tens to hundreds of gigabytes before tile artefacts.

findings.title: Exact PSGA cache and derived-output conditions
findings.statement: These must be confirmed against the organisation’s current OS agreements and selected products before any protected cache is loaded.

findings.title: Actual departmental landing zone
findings.statement: Azure is the default recommendation, but the sponsoring organisation’s approved cloud, network and monitoring services may change deployment details.

findings.title: Enterprise-managed authorisation host support
findings.statement: MCP EMA is stable as an extension, but end-to-end support must be tested for each target host and enterprise identity environment.

findings.title: Formal clearance for Locus Accord
findings.statement: Preliminary search found no exact GitHub repository conflict, but package registries, domains, UKIPO and common-law product usage require formal checks.

findings.title: Preserve temporal identifiers
findings.statement: UPRN, BLPU, USRN, TOID, OSID and ONS geography codes need source, namespace, validity interval, successor/predecessor relations and provider-native attributes.

findings.title: Use WGS84 for interchange and EPSG:27700 for GB metric work
findings.statement: Record source CRS, axis order, transformation operation/software and output CRS. Do not silently convert coordinates.

findings.title: Govern emergency controls across registry, credentials, agents and evidence
findings.statement: Suspension must include service/tool registry, credential revocation, workflow cancellation, cache quarantine, agent quarantine, evidence freeze and rollback.

findings.title: Keep the public pack usable without JavaScript
findings.statement: The static site should progressively enhance a readable HTML/Markdown evidence pack, with keyboard operation and WCAG 2.2 AA acceptance tests.

findings.title: Use an integrated OpenAI/development workflow
findings.statement: Use Deep Research for current evidence, GitHub-connected analysis for repositories, this static pack for decisions, Codex for staged implementation, and Codex Security after code exists. No newer single capability replaces the evidence-synthesis role.
